posts.title: DJI Mini 4 Pro vs Mini 5 Pro: Which Mini Drone Should You Buy?
posts.summary: The Mini 5 Pro adds a 1-inch sensor and a rotating gimbal. Is it worth the upgrade over the Mini 4 Pro? Camera, safety, size and value compared.
posts.body:
The DJI Mini 4 Pro and Mini 5 Pro are the two best mini camera drones you can buy in Lebanon. Both fold into a small bag, both sense obstacles in every direction, and both shoot excellent 4K. So which one makes sense for you?

## Quick verdict

- **Choose the Mini 4 Pro** if you want a proven, lighter pro-level drone at a lower price.
- **Choose the Mini 5 Pro** if image quality in low light matters most, or you shoot a lot of vertical and creative angles.

## Camera

This is the big difference. The **Mini 5 Pro** uses a **1-inch 50 MP sensor**, the largest ever in a DJI Mini, with 4K video up to 120 fps. The **Mini 4 Pro** has a **1/1.3-inch 48 MP sensor** with 4K/60fps HDR and 4K/100fps slow motion. In daylight both look great; at sunset, at night and in high-contrast scenes like the Lebanese coast at golden hour, the Mini 5 Pro holds more detail and less noise.

## Gimbal and vertical video

Both shoot true vertical video for Reels and TikTok. The **Mini 5 Pro** goes further with a gimbal that rotates well beyond 90°, so you can get tilted, creative shots without editing.

## Safety

Both have omnidirectional obstacle sensing and ActiveTrack. The **Mini 5 Pro** adds a forward **LiDAR** sensor, which helps in low light when cameras struggle.

## Weight and rules

The Mini 4 Pro stays under 249 g. The Mini 5 Pro sits right around the 250 g mark depending on the region and battery. In Lebanon every flight needs an Army permit regardless of weight, so this matters less here than in Europe. Read our [drone laws guide](/blog/drone-laws-in-lebanon.html).

## Which one should you buy?

If you are starting out or want the best value, the **Mini 4 Pro** is still one of the best drones ever made. If you are a content creator or photographer who wants the best camera in a small drone, the **Mini 5 Pro** is worth it.

See the [DJI Mini 4 Pro in Lebanon](/dji-mini-4-pro-lebanon.html) and [DJI Mini 5 Pro in Lebanon](/dji-mini-5-pro-lebanon.html) pages, or message us on WhatsApp for current prices and availability.

posts.title: DJI Avata 2 vs Avata 360: Which FPV Drone Is Right for You?
posts.summary: Classic FPV flying or 8K 360° capture? We compare the DJI Avata 2 and Avata 360 on camera, flight time, ease of use and who each one suits.
posts.body:
The DJI Avata 2 and Avata 360 are both FPV drones you fly with goggles and the RC Motion 3, but they film in very different ways.

## Quick verdict

- **Choose the Avata 2** for classic cinematic FPV: dives, flips and fly-throughs with a lighter, simpler drone.
- **Choose the Avata 360** if you want to capture everything around you and pick the angle later.

## Camera

The **Avata 2** has a single 1/1.3-inch camera shooting 4K/60fps HDR with a wide 155° view. The **Avata 360** uses two 1/1.1-inch sensors to record **8K/60fps HDR 360° video** and 120 MP 360° photos, and can switch to a single-lens 4K mode.

With the Avata 360 you don't have to aim the camera while flying: you reframe in editing, so one flight over Jounieh bay or a mountain road gives you many different shots.

## Flight and handling

- **Avata 2:** about 377 g and up to about 23 minutes per battery, with one-push flips and rolls (Easy ACRO).
- **Avata 360:** about 455 g and up to about 23 minutes per battery, with omnidirectional sensing in 360° mode and forward LiDAR.

The Avata 2 feels more agile. The Avata 360 is heavier but safer around obstacles in 360° mode.

## Who should buy which?

- **Avata 2:** hobby FPV pilots, travel videos, action and sports clips.
- **Avata 360:** wedding and event videographers, real estate, tourism content, and anyone who hates missing the shot.

## Accessories you'll want

Both benefit from protection frames and landing gear. The Avata 360 needs **side protection** for its two lenses. See [Avata 2 accessories](/dji-avata-2-lebanon.html) and [Avata 360 accessories](/dji-avata-360-lebanon.html).

Remember that drone flights in Lebanon need an Army permit; read our [drone laws guide](/blog/drone-laws-in-lebanon.html).

posts.title: DJI Lito X1 vs Mini 4 Pro: Best Beginner Camera Drone?
posts.summary: DJI’s new beginner Lito X1 against the popular Mini 4 Pro: camera, safety sensors, flight time and which one a first-time pilot should choose.
posts.body:
The DJI Lito X1 is DJI's newest drone for beginners, while the Mini 4 Pro has been the go-to mini camera drone for years. Both are around 249 g with obstacle sensing in every direction. Here's how to choose.

## Quick verdict

- **Choose the Lito X1** if you are a first-time pilot who wants the latest safety features and simple flying.
- **Choose the Mini 4 Pro** if you want more advanced camera modes and tracking for creative work.

## Camera

Both use a **1/1.3-inch 48 MP sensor**. The **Lito X1** shoots 4K/60fps HDR, 4K up to 100 fps and 2.7K vertical, with D-Log M colour. The **Mini 4 Pro** shoots 4K/60fps HDR, 4K/100fps slow motion and true vertical shooting with its rotating gimbal. Image quality is very close.

## Safety

Both have omnidirectional obstacle sensing. The **Lito X1** adds a forward **LiDAR** sensor, which helps in low light. The **Mini 4 Pro** has ActiveTrack 360° for advanced subject tracking.

## Flight time and storage

- **Lito X1:** up to 36 minutes per battery and 42 GB internal storage.
- **Mini 4 Pro:** up to 34 minutes per battery (45 with the Plus battery), recording to a microSD card.

## Which one for you?

For a first drone, the **Lito X1** is the easiest and safest choice. If you already know you want to film creatively, track cars or bikes, and grow into more advanced shots, the **Mini 4 Pro** gives you more room.

See the [DJI Lito X1](/dji-lito-x1-lebanon.html) and [DJI Mini 4 Pro](/dji-mini-4-pro-lebanon.html) pages, and our [best beginner drone guide](/blog/best-beginner-drone-to-buy-in-lebanon.html).

posts.title: Best Drone for Wedding and Event Filming in Lebanon
posts.summary: Planning to film weddings, parties or events with a drone in Lebanon? The best DJI drones for the job, the permit you need and tips for great shots.
posts.body:
Drone shots have become a must at Lebanese weddings, from venue fly-overs to the entrance and the zaffe. Here are the drones we recommend for event work, and what you need to know before you fly.

## First: the permit

In Lebanon, event filming with a drone needs a permit from the Lebanese Army. In 2026, exceptional permits have been granted for events such as weddings, with the locations and times stated in advance. Apply early. Read our full [drone laws guide](/blog/drone-laws-in-lebanon.html).

## Best drones for weddings and events

### DJI Mini 4 Pro: best all-rounder

Small, quiet and with obstacle sensing in every direction, the [Mini 4 Pro](/dji-mini-4-pro-lebanon.html) is safe to fly near venues and guests, and its 4K HDR video handles bright sun and evening lights well.

### DJI Mini 5 Pro: best image quality

The 1-inch sensor of the [Mini 5 Pro](/dji-mini-5-pro-lebanon.html) shines in the evening, when most wedding receptions happen. Ideal if you sell your footage professionally.

### DJI Avata 360: most creative

The [Avata 360](/dji-avata-360-lebanon.html) records 8K 360° video, so you can capture the whole scene in one pass and choose the angle in editing. Perfect for dramatic venue reveals.

### DJI Avata 2: indoor and fly-through shots

For flying through a venue or following the couple, the [Avata 2](/dji-avata-2-lebanon.html) with its built-in guards is the classic FPV choice. Only fly indoors with an experienced pilot.

## Tips for great event footage

- Scout the venue before the day and plan your take-off spot.
- Keep a safe distance from guests and never fly directly over people.
- Bring at least three batteries; a Fly More Combo is a must.
- Use ND filters for daytime outdoor ceremonies.
- Agree with the couple and the venue before filming.

Need advice on the right drone for your events business? Message us on WhatsApp or browse [all DJI drones for sale in Lebanon](/dji-drones-lebanon.html).

posts.title: Buying a Used DJI Drone in Lebanon: What to Check
posts.summary: A used DJI drone can save you a lot of money. Here is exactly what to check before you buy: battery health, gimbal, motors, activation and more.
posts.body:
A used DJI drone is a smart way to save money in Lebanon, but only if it has been checked properly. Here is what to look at before you pay, whether you buy from us or anyone else.

## 1. Battery health

Batteries are the most expensive part to replace. In the DJI Fly app, check each battery's **cycle count** and **health**. Swollen batteries, or batteries that drop quickly in flight, should be replaced.

## 2. Gimbal and camera

Power on the drone and watch the gimbal calibrate. It should move smoothly without noise or shaking. Record a short video and check that the horizon is level and the image is sharp, without spots or scratches on the lens.

## 3. Motors and propellers

Spin each motor by hand: it should turn freely and quietly. Look for cracked, chipped or bent propellers and arms.

## 4. Crash history

Check the body for cracks, glue or new screws. Ask the seller directly if it has crashed. The flight records in the app also show past flights.

## 5. Activation and account

Make sure the drone is **unlinked from the previous owner's DJI account** so you can activate it, and update the firmware.

## 6. What's in the box

Confirm the controller, cables, charger and extra batteries match the listing, especially for Fly More Combos.

## 7. Test flight

Ask for a short test flight, or at least a video of the exact drone flying, hovering steadily and returning home.

## Why buy used from Drone Zone?

Every used drone we sell is checked before sale: battery health, gimbal, motors, propellers and firmware. The condition is written on the listing and we're happy to send extra photos or a flight video on WhatsApp.

See [all DJI drones in stock](/dji-drones-lebanon.html), new and used.

posts.title: Drone Laws in Lebanon (2026): Permits, Rules and No-Fly Areas
posts.summary: Do you need a permit to fly a drone in Lebanon? Who issues it, what documents you need, the 2026 restrictions and where you should never fly.
posts.body:
In Lebanon, every drone flight needs a permit from the Lebanese Army. This guide explains how the system works as of October 2026. Rules change often here, so always check with the Army before you fly.

## Who issues drone permits in Lebanon?

Drone filming permits are issued by the **Lebanese Army Command (Directorate of Orientation)**, not by municipalities. There is no national drone register: instead, you apply for a permit for each filming job, with the places and dates you plan to fly.

- **Cost:** no fee has been reported.
- **Time:** allow at least one week, and apply well in advance for events.
- **How to apply:** by email, by fax, or in person at the Army Command. Check the official [Lebanese Army website](https://www.lebarmy.gov.lb) for the current contact details.

## What you need to apply

- A signed request explaining the purpose of the flight, the drone and camera models with serial numbers, the locations and dates, and your phone number
- Photos of the drone clearly showing the serial number
- A copy of your Lebanese ID (or passport with entry stamp for visitors)
- Any pilot licence or drone certificate you hold

## The situation in 2026

- **March 2026:** the Army suspended drone filming permits across Lebanon until further notice.
- **June 2026:** exceptional permits restarted for **events only**, such as weddings and cultural or sports events. You must state the locations and times in advance, and several events can be combined in one request.
- Ordinary landscape or tourism filming was not being permitted at the time of writing.

Before any flight, contact the Army to check what is allowed on your date and location.

## Where you should never fly

- Over or near **military bases, barracks and checkpoints**. The Army can confiscate or bring down drones there, even with a permit.
- Near **Beirut airport** or any airfield.
- Over **security facilities** or government buildings.
- In the **South** and border areas, where a civilian drone can be mistaken for a military one.
- Over crowds, during fireworks or in clouds.

## Privacy: filming people

Filming people who can be identified can fall under Lebanon's personal data law (Law 81/2018). Always ask permission before filming private property, homes, weddings or people, and don't publish footage of strangers without their consent.

## FAQ

### Do I need a permit to fly a small drone under 249 g in Lebanon?

Yes. Lebanon does not have a weight exemption like Europe or the US, so the permit rules apply to mini drones too.

Looking for a drone for events or weddings? See [all DJI drones we sell in Lebanon](/dji-drones-lebanon.html).

posts.title: DJI Neo 2 vs DJI Flip: Which Should You Buy?
posts.summary: Two palm-launch DJI drones for selfies and vlogs. We compare camera, flight time, safety, size and price in Lebanon to help you choose.
posts.body:
The DJI Neo 2 and DJI Flip are both made for people who want to film themselves: you launch them from your hand and they follow you automatically. But they are quite different drones. Here's how they compare.

## Quick verdict

- **Choose the DJI Neo 2** if you want the smallest, lightest drone for selfies, sports and FPV fun.
- **Choose the DJI Flip** if image quality and flight time matter most, especially for travel and sunset shots.

## Camera and video

The **Flip** has a much larger **1/1.3-inch 48 MP sensor** with 4K/60fps HDR video, so it handles sunsets, shadows and low light far better. The **Neo 2** uses a smaller **1/2-inch 12 MP sensor**, but it now has a 2-axis gimbal and shoots 4K up to 100 fps, which is great for slow motion.

## Size and weight

- **Neo 2:** about 151 g, truly pocket-sized
- **Flip:** under 249 g, folds flat but is noticeably bigger

## Safety and obstacle avoidance

The **Flip** has full-coverage propeller guards, so it is very safe to fly close to people. The **Neo 2** also has guards and adds a forward **LiDAR** sensor to avoid obstacles in front of it.

## Flight time

- **Neo 2:** up to about 19 minutes per battery
- **Flip:** up to about 31 minutes per battery

For a day trip, the Flip needs fewer battery swaps. Either way, a Fly More Combo with three batteries is worth it.

## Control options

Both can be flown from your palm with gestures or the app. The **Neo 2** can also be flown with DJI goggles and the RC Motion 3 for immersive FPV flight, which the Flip doesn't support.

## Price in Lebanon

The Neo 2 is usually the cheaper of the two, while the Flip costs more but gives you a bigger sensor and longer flights. Prices change with each new shipment, so message us on WhatsApp for the latest price of both.

## Our recommendation

For most people who mainly film themselves and their friends, the **Neo 2** is the more fun and portable choice. If you want the best footage from a small, safe drone, the **Flip** is worth the extra size.

See the [DJI Neo 2 page](/dji-neo-2-lebanon.html) and the [DJI Flip page](/dji-flip-lebanon.html) for combos and accessories, and remember to check the [drone rules in Lebanon](/blog/drone-laws-in-lebanon.html) before you fly.

posts.title: How to Choose Your First Drone: A Step-by-Step Guide
posts.summary: FPV or cinematic, beginner or experienced: a step-by-step guide to picking the right first drone, from speed and camera to safety and controllers.
posts.body:
Buying your first drone can feel overwhelming. FPV, cinematic, beginner, pro — what does it all mean? This guide walks you through every decision, one step at a time.

## Step 1: Decide What You Want to Do

Ask yourself: **Do I want to fly for fun, or film beautiful footage?**

- **FPV (First-Person View):** You wear goggles and fly like you're in the cockpit. Fast, immersive, thrilling. Great for indoor flying and freestyle.
- **Cinematic:** You want smooth, stable, high-quality video. Great for travel, landscapes, and vlogs.
- **Both:** Some drones can do both — like the **DJI Neo** with the right accessories.

![FPV setup: DJI Avata 2 with goggles and motion controller](/images/uploads/dz-blog-fpv-gear.webp)

FPV: drone, goggles and motion controller (DJI Avata 2) · Image: DJI

![Cinematic aerial shot of riders crossing a river](/images/uploads/dz-blog-cinematic-shot.webp)

Cinematic: smooth, stable aerial footage (DJI Mini 4 Pro) · Image: DJI

## Step 2: Match the Drone to Your Experience Level

- **Total beginner:** Look for palm takeoff, automatic shots, and propeller guards. The **DJI Neo** is the easiest starting point.
- **Some experience:** You want better camera quality, longer flight time, and more speed. The **DJI Mini 4 Pro** or **Lito series** are great next steps.
- **Ready for FPV:** You want goggles, a motion controller, and serious speed. The **DJI Avata 2** is a dedicated FPV drone built for agile, fast flight.

## Step 3: Consider Speed and Performance

Speed matters depending on your goals. Here are the **Sport mode speeds** for every drone in this guide:

- **DJI Neo:** Max horizontal speed of **28.8 km/h** in Sport mode.
- **DJI Mini 4 Pro:** Max horizontal speed of **57.6 km/h** in Sport mode.
- **DJI Lito Series (Lito 1 & Lito X1):** Max horizontal speed of **64.8 km/h** in Sport mode.
- **DJI Avata 2:** Max horizontal speed of **57.6 km/h** in Sport mode, and up to **97.2 km/h** in Manual mode for experienced FPV pilots.

## Step 4: Camera and Video Quality

- **Beginner:** 4K/30fps is plenty. Neo delivers this.
- **Intermediate:** Look for 4K/60fps, HDR, and larger sensors. Mini 4 Pro and Lito X1 offer this.
- **Advanced:** 10-bit D-Log M, 8K, and adjustable aperture. Lito X1 and higher-end models.

## Step 5: Flight Time and Range

- **DJI Neo:** 12–14 minutes of flight time.
- **Mini 4 Pro and Lito series:** 30+ minutes.
- **FPV range:** Depends on goggles and controller. The Avata 2 and Neo FPV Combo work well for close-range immersion.

## Step 6: Safety Features

- **Obstacle avoidance:** Mini 4 Pro and Lito series have omnidirectional sensing.
- **LiDAR:** Some advanced drones use LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) for highly precise obstacle detection and terrain mapping. It's a step up from standard sensors.
- **Propeller guards:** Neo has full guards — safe indoors and around people.
- **Return-to-home:** Essential for beginners. Most modern DJI drones include it.

## Step 7: Controller and Goggles

- **Phone only:** Neo can fly with just your phone.
- **Standard controller or RC2 controller:** Mini 4 Pro and Lito series come with either the standard controller or the RC2 controller. The **RC2 has a built-in screen**.
- **FPV goggles:** Needed for immersive flight. DJI Goggles N3 + Motion 3 work with Neo, and the Avata 2 comes with its own FPV setup.

## Step 8: Budget and Accessories

Think about extra batteries, carrying cases, and protection. [DroneZoneLB.com](./) stocks accessories like camera protection, roll cages, landing gear, and AirTag mounts.

## Step 9: Where to Buy

Choose a trusted local seller who can support you after the purchase. **[DroneZoneLB.com](./)** offers the drones and accessories mentioned in this guide.

posts.title: Every DJI Drone Explained: A Complete Guide to Choosing Your Perfect Model
posts.summary: From the palm-sized Neo to the flagship Mavic 4 Pro: key specs, who each DJI drone suits, and the downsides to know before you buy.
posts.body:
At **DroneZoneLB.com**, we carry a wide range of DJI drones — from palm-sized beginner drones to professional dual-camera and flagship models. But with so many options available, it can be difficult to know which drone is right for you.

This guide breaks down every DJI drone in our range, including the key features, who each model is best suited for, and the potential downsides you should know before buying.

## Quick Comparison Table

![DJI drones quick comparison table](/images/uploads/dz-blog-dji-comparison-table.webp)

## DJI Neo: The Beginner's Best Friend

![DJI Neo](/images/uploads/dz-blog-neo.webp)

DJI Neo · Image: DJI

The **DJI Neo** is DJI's simplest and most accessible camera drone. At just 135 g, it can take off and land from your palm and can be flown without a traditional remote controller.

Its built-in propeller guards and automated flight modes make it particularly appealing to beginners and casual users.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** 135 g
- **Max Speed:** 28.8 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 18 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/2-inch CMOS, 12 MP
- **Video:** Up to 4K/30fps
- **Gimbal:** Single-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O4
- **Internal Storage:** 22 GB
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** No
- **Wind Resistance:** Level 4
- **Palm Takeoff and Landing:** Yes
- **QuickShots:** Yes
- **Subject Tracking:** Yes
- **MicroSD:** No

**Who it's for:** Total beginners, casual users and creators who want an extremely simple drone that can take off from their hand.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **Wind sensitivity** — the lightweight body can struggle in gusty conditions.
- **Short battery life** — real-world flight time can be considerably lower than the 18-minute maximum.
- **No microSD slot** — footage is stored in the 22 GB internal memory.
- **No conventional obstacle avoidance**.
- **Noisy** compared with traditional Mini drones.
- **Limited range with phone control** compared with using a dedicated DJI remote controller.

## DJI Neo 2: The Improved Selfie Drone

![DJI Neo 2](/images/uploads/dz-blog-neo-2.webp)

DJI Neo 2 · Image: DJI

The **DJI Neo 2** takes the original Neo concept and adds significant upgrades while remaining extremely compact.

It is faster, has more internal storage, improved stabilization, better tracking and omnidirectional obstacle sensing.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** 151 g
- **Max Speed:** 43.2 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 19 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/2-inch sensor
- **Video:** Up to 4K/60fps
- **Slow Motion:** Up to 4K/100fps
- **Gimbal:** 2-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O4
- **Internal Storage:** 49 GB
- **Obstacle Sensing:** Omnidirectional
- **Tracking:** ActiveTrack
- **Gesture Control:** Yes
- **Palm Takeoff and Landing:** Yes

**Who it's for:** Beginners and creators who want a small follow-me drone with more advanced tracking and obstacle sensing.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **Battery life is still short** compared with the Mini series.
- **1/2-inch sensor** is smaller than the sensors used on the Mini 5 Pro, Lito X1 and larger Air and Mavic models.
- **Internal storage only** — there is no microSD slot.
- **Cannot shoot RAW photos**.

## DJI Lito 1: A Newer Mini 3, Done Right

![DJI Lito 1](/images/uploads/dz-blog-lito-1.webp)

DJI Lito 1 · Image: DJI

The **DJI Lito 1** takes many of the strengths of the Mini 3 and adds features that the Mini 3 lacks, especially omnidirectional obstacle sensing and newer O4 transmission.

It is faster than the Mini 3 and adds more advanced tracking and obstacle detection while maintaining a compact sub-249 g design.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** Under 249 g
- **Max Speed:** 64.8 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 36 minutes
- **Plus Battery:** Up to 52 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/2-inch CMOS, 48 MP
- **Video:** Up to 4K/60fps
- **Slow Motion:** 4K/100fps
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O4
- **Internal Storage:** None
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** Omnidirectional
- **Tracking:** ActiveTrack
- **Vertical Shooting:** Yes
- **RAW Photos:** Yes
- **MicroSD:** Required
- **Photos:** Up to 8K

**Who it's for:** Anyone considering a Mini 3 who wants modern obstacle sensing, faster flight and newer transmission technology.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **No internal storage** — a microSD card is required.
- **Smaller 1/2-inch sensor** than the Lito X1 and Mini 5 Pro.
- **Digital zoom quality deteriorates noticeably** at higher magnification.
- The Plus battery takes the drone above the sub-249 g class.

## DJI Lito X1: A Newer Mini 4 Pro, and Better

![DJI Lito X1](/images/uploads/dz-blog-lito-x1.webp)

DJI Lito X1 · Image: DJI

The **DJI Lito X1** is a premium lightweight camera drone with a 1/1.3-inch sensor, O4 transmission, 10-bit D-Log M and advanced obstacle sensing.

It also adds forward-facing LiDAR and 42 GB of internal storage, making it one of the most feature-packed drones in its class.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** Under 249 g
- **Max Speed:** 64.8 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 36 minutes
- **Plus Battery:** Up to 52 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/1.3-inch CMOS
- **Video:** Up to 4K/60fps HDR
- **Slow Motion:** Up to 4K/100fps
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O4
- **Internal Storage:** 42 GB
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** Omnidirectional
- **LiDAR:** Forward-facing
- **Color:** 10-bit D-Log M
- **RAW Photos:** Yes
- **Vertical Shooting:** 2.7K
- **Tracking:** ActiveTrack

**Who it's for:** Creators who want professional-style features, advanced obstacle sensing and high image quality in a compact drone.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **Vertical shooting is limited to 2.7K**.

## DJI Mini 2: The Classic Entry-Level Drone

![DJI Mini 2](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-2.webp)

DJI Mini 2 · Image: DJI

The **DJI Mini 2** was one of the drones that established the modern DJI Mini category. It remains capable of 4K video while weighing only 242 g.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** 242 g
- **Max Speed:** 57.6 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 31 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/2.3-inch CMOS, 12 MP
- **Video:** Up to 4K/30fps
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O2
- **Internal Storage:** None
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** No
- **Wind Resistance:** Level 5
- **QuickShots:** Yes
- **RAW Photos:** Yes
- **MicroSD:** Required

**Who it's for:** Buyers on a budget who want a proven DJI drone with 4K video.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **No obstacle avoidance sensors**, so you need to be extra careful in tight spaces.
- **Older O2 transmission** compared with newer O4 drones.
- **Older hardware and software platform** than current Mini models.
- **No internal storage**.
- Some users report connection issues even at relatively short distances.

## DJI Mini 2 SE & Mini 4K: Essentially the Same Drone

![DJI Mini 2 SE and Mini 4K](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-4k.webp)

DJI Mini 2 SE and Mini 4K · Image: DJI

The **DJI Mini 2 SE and DJI Mini 4K are essentially the same drone platform**.

The Mini 4K is best thought of as the **4K version of the Mini 2 SE**, rather than a completely new generation. They use the same basic aircraft, camera sensor, 3-axis gimbal, O2 transmission and battery system.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** 246 g
- **Max Speed:** 57.6 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 31 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/2.3-inch CMOS, 12 MP
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O2
- **Internal Storage:** None
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** No
- **MicroSD:** Required
- **Mini 2 SE Video:** Up to 2.7K/30fps
- **Mini 4K Video:** Up to 4K/30fps
- **Mini 4K Bitrate:** Up to 100 Mbps

**Who it's for:** Beginners looking for an affordable traditional DJI camera drone.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **No obstacle avoidance**.
- **Older O2 transmission**.
- **1/2.3-inch sensor** is noticeably smaller than the sensor in the Mini 3 and newer models.
- **No internal storage**.
- The Mini 2 SE is limited to 2.7K, making the **Mini 4K the better choice when the price difference is small**.
- Both models lack the advanced tracking and sensing available on newer DJI drones.
- **Limited range in difficult environments** compared with newer O4 models.

### Bottom Line

The **Mini 4K is essentially a rebranded Mini 2 SE with 4K video capability**. It should therefore be considered part of the same platform rather than a completely separate generation.

## DJI Mini 3: The Long-Flight Mini

![DJI Mini 3](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-3.webp)

DJI Mini 3 · Image: DJI

The **DJI Mini 3** stands out for its impressive battery life and excellent image quality in a lightweight package.

With the standard battery, it can fly for up to 38 minutes, while the Plus battery extends this to 51 minutes.

### Key Features

- **Weight:** 248 g
- **Max Speed:** 57.6 km/h in Sport mode
- **Flight Time:** Up to 38 minutes
- **Plus Battery:** Up to 51 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/1.3-inch CMOS, 48 MP
- **Video:** Up to 4K HDR
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O2
- **Internal Storage:** None
- **Obstacle Avoidance:** No
- **Vertical Shooting:** Yes
- **RAW Photos:** Yes
- **MicroSD:** Required

**Who it's for:** Pilots who prioritize flight time, portability and good image quality.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **No obstacle avoidance sensors** — this is the biggest limitation compared with the Mini 3 Pro.
- **Drifts in a light breeze** — its low weight can make it less stable in windy conditions.
- **No 4K/60fps or D-Cinelike colour** — video options are more limited than the Pro and newer Mini models.
- **Older O2 transmission** — newer O4 drones offer a significant improvement in connectivity and interference resistance.
- **No Follow Me function** — the Mini 3 does not have ActiveTrack.
- **No internal storage** — a microSD card is required.

## DJI Mini 3 Pro: The Advanced Mini

![DJI Mini 3 Pro](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-3-pro.webp)

DJI Mini 3 Pro · Image: DJI

The **DJI Mini 3 Pro** introduced obstacle sensing, 4K/60fps video and O3 transmission to the Mini series while keeping the aircraft below 249 g with the standard battery.

- **Weight:** 249 g
- **Max Speed:** 57.6 km/h in Sport mode

- **Plus Battery:** Up to 47 minutes
- **Camera:** 1/1.3-inch CMOS, 48 MP
- **Video:** Up to 4K/60fps
- **Gimbal:** 3-axis mechanical
- **Transmission:** O3
- **Internal Storage:** 1.2 GB
- **Obstacle Sensing:** Forward, backward and downward
- **Vertical Shooting:** Yes
- **RAW Photos:** Yes
- **D-Cinelike:** Yes
- **ActiveTrack:** Yes

**Who it's for:** Beginners and experienced pilots who want a more advanced Mini with obstacle sensing and smarter flight features.

### Potential Downsides to Consider

- **48 MP photo mode is sluggish** — there is no burst or auto-bracketing, and saving high-resolution photos can take time.
- **No side obstacle sensors** — obstacle avoidance does not cover every direction
- **Limited range** compared with newer DJI drones.
- **Older O3 transmission** compared with the O4 systems on newer Mini models.

## DJI Mini 4 Pro: The Complete Mini

![DJI Mini 4 Pro](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-4-pro.webp)

DJI Mini 4 Pro · Image: DJI

## DJI Mini 5 Pro: The Professional Mini

![DJI Mini 5 Pro](/images/uploads/dz-blog-mini-5-pro.webp)

DJI Mini 5 Pro · Image: DJI

The **DJI Mini 5 Pro** is the biggest camera upgrade the Mini series has received, introducing a **1-inch CMOS sensor** while keeping the aircraft around the 250 g mark.

It combines flagship-style image quality with advanced obstacle sensing, LiDAR and O4+ transmission.

### ⚠️ Known Issue Alert — Propeller Mounting System

The Mini 5 Pro introduced a new **quick-release propeller mounting system**, which is easier to use but has been linked to reports of **propellers detaching during flight**.

Multiple users have reported sudden crashes where a propeller detached, causing the drone to lose stability and fall from the sky. In some cases, warnings such as **"Motor Overloaded"** or **"Propulsion System Error"** appeared before the crash.

DJI advises owners to inspect the propellers before every flight and make sure the propellers and motors are properly secured.

## DJI Avata 360: The 360° FPV Experience

![DJI Avata 360](/images/uploads/dz-blog-avata-360.webp)

posts.title: What to Do Before You Fly: A Pre-Flight Checklist for Drone Pilots
posts.summary: Batteries, propellers, firmware, weather, GPS and the law: a simple pre-flight checklist to keep your drone safe and every flight smooth.
posts.body:
A great flight starts on the ground. Most crashes, flyaways and lost drones happen because of something that could have been caught in two minutes before takeoff. Run through this checklist every time you fly — beginner or pro.

## 1. Check the Rules First

- Stay away from airports, military areas, government buildings, crowds and private property.

## 2. Charge Everything the Night Before

![Charging drone batteries, controller and phone at home](/images/uploads/dz-blog-preflight-batteries.webp)

Charge everything the night before

- **Drone batteries** — fully charged, no swelling, cracks or damage. Never fly a puffed battery.
- **Remote controller** and **phone or goggles**.
- Bring spare batteries if you have them — flights always feel shorter than you expect.

## 3. Update Firmware and Apps at Home

Open the DJI Fly app (or your drone's app) on Wi-Fi at home and install any firmware updates for the drone, controller and batteries. An update in the field can take 20+ minutes and drain your batteries.

## 4. Inspect Your Drone

![Pilot inspecting drone propellers before flight](/images/uploads/dz-blog-preflight-inspection.webp)

Check props, gimbal and lens before every flight

- **Propellers:** no chips, cracks or bends. Replace damaged props — they're cheap, crashes aren't.
- **Props secure:** correctly matched and locked onto the right motors.
- **Gimbal:** remove the gimbal cover/protector before powering on.
- **Camera lens and sensors:** clean and free of dust or fingerprints.
- **Memory card:** inserted, with enough free space.

## 5. Check the Weather

- **Wind:** small drones like the DJI Neo or Mini series struggle in strong wind, especially at altitude and near the coast.
- **Rain and fog:** most consumer drones are not waterproof — don't fly in rain.
- **Temperature:** batteries drain faster in the cold and can overheat in strong summer heat.

## 6. Choose a Safe Takeoff Spot

![Drone hovering above a landing pad in an open field](/images/uploads/dz-blog-preflight-takeoff.webp)

Take off from an open, flat spot with a landing pad

- Open area, away from trees, power lines, people and animals.
- Flat surface for takeoff and landing — use a landing pad on sand, grass or dust.
- Keep the drone in your line of sight at all times.

## 7. Set Up the App Before Takeoff

- **Return-to-Home (RTH) altitude:** set it higher than the tallest obstacle around you.
- **Wait for GPS lock** and make sure the Home Point is recorded before you take off.
- Calibrate the compass if the app asks — away from cars and metal.
- Check that obstacle avoidance is on (if your drone has it).

## 8. Do a Short Hover Test

Take off to about 2 metres and hover for 10–20 seconds. Check that the drone is stable, the controls respond correctly and there are no strange sounds or warnings. All good? Now enjoy your flight.

## Quick Checklist

- ✅ Rules checked / permission
- ✅ Batteries, controller and phone charged
- ✅ Firmware updated
- ✅ Props, gimbal cover, lens, SD card
- ✅ Weather and wind OK
- ✅ Safe, open takeoff spot
- ✅ RTH altitude set, GPS locked
- ✅ Hover test done

posts.title: Must-Have Accessories for Your DJI Mini Drone
posts.summary: Propeller guards, cases, landing gear, sunhoods and more: the accessories that protect your DJI Mini and make every flight easier.
posts.body:
You just got a DJI Mini. It flies beautifully, it fits in your hand, and it cost real money. The right accessories keep it safe, make it easier to carry, and help you get better footage. Here are the ones we recommend for the **Mini 2 / 2SE / 4K, Mini 3 / 3 Pro, Mini 4 Pro and Mini 5 Pro**.

## 1. Propeller Guards

The single most useful accessory for new pilots. Guards stop the propellers from hitting trees, walls and people, and they save you from bent props after a light bump. Use them for your first flights, indoors, or close to obstacles.

- **Tip:** guards add a little weight and catch more wind. Fly them on calm days and expect slightly shorter flight time.
- Want to fly at dusk? Our **glow-in-the-dark guards** make the drone easy to spot in low light.

## 2. A Proper Carry Case

Most damage happens in the bag, not in the air. A shaped case holds the drone, controller and batteries in place so the gimbal and arms don't get knocked around. Pick a **drone + controller case** if you carry everything together, or a compact one if you travel light.

## 3. Landing Gear

Landing gear lifts the drone a few centimetres off the ground. That keeps sand, dust and wet grass away from the camera and motors, and makes taking off from beaches, rocks or uneven mountain ground much safer.

## 4. Gimbal and Camera Protection

The gimbal is the most fragile (and most expensive) part of your Mini. A gimbal cover or camera protector clips on during transport and comes off in seconds before you fly. Never take off with it on.

## 5. Propeller Clips

Small but important. Clips hold the folded propellers together so they don't bend or crack in your bag, and they make packing faster.

## 6. Controller Sunhood

In the Lebanese sun, your controller screen can be almost impossible to read. A sunhood for the **DJI RC 2** or **RC-N1** blocks the glare so you can actually see your shot and your battery level.

## 7. Battery Accessories

A battery holder keeps spare batteries organised and protected, and a battery removal tool (Mini 2 / 2SE / 4K) makes swapping easier. For longer flights on the Mini 3 / 4 Pro, ask us about the **Battery Plus**. Remember to check your local weight rules before using it.

## 8. AirTag / Smart Tag Mount

If your drone ever goes down in a valley or a field, a tracker can be the difference between finding it and losing it. The mount holds an AirTag or smart tag securely without blocking sensors.

## 9. Just for Fun: Stands and Payload Baskets

A stand turns your drone into a display piece on your desk when it's not flying. A small payload basket lets you drop very light items for fun. Only carry tiny loads, keep away from people, and never fly over crowds.

## Our Starter Kit Recommendation

If you only buy three things: **propeller guards, a carry case and a controller sunhood**. Add landing gear if you fly on beaches or in the mountains.
